recaps.title: Week 1 Recap: TTAB Hits the Lottery, Jacob’s First Win, Slumlords Get Off the Bus
recaps.dateLabel: Tuesday drop · Week 1 finals locked after MNF
recaps.coldOpen: Welcome back to IDP country, where 220 is a Tuesday, 315 is a war crime, and Monday night still flips scoreboards like a light switch. Week 1’s thesis was simple: premium draft capital does not equal points, Fantrax IDP math is a rumor, and the only board that mattered was the one still alive after Monday. We got a kitty jackpot, a Survivor eviction, Jacob Crisp’s first Wheels Up win, and enough goose eggs from “safe” stars to stock a diner. Hero of the week: whoever waited until after MNF to write the recap — and T.J. Watt’s 52. Goat of the week: Fantrax projections, Aga’s top-3, and the Host’s Waddle flex.
heroes: TTAB’s 315 — Allen 45 / Watson 44 / Jeanty 41 / Baun 35; kitty locked
Jacob Crisp’s first WU win — Hyper 259.5 over Dongers 246.5 (Monday heist; Walker 48)
T.J. Watt 52 (Goats) — half-century IDP and a 254 close
Gesicki 23 (Saltese) — no-name TE beat Bill’s premium room
goats: Slumlords 176.5 — Survivor Week 1; London 4 / Pickens 5 / Fannin 5; off the bus
Aga’s top-3 (Ultron) — Chase 3 / Cook 10 / Loveland 0 (plus Garrett 0)
Eddies’ TE tax — Gesicki 23 vs Warren 12 + Pitts 0
The Host’s Waddle — started flex, scored 1
Dongers 246.5 — lost a game they thought they’d already won

matchups.blurb: Chase didn’t win Week 1 so much as commit a hate crime against the format. While half the league was still arguing about projections, TTAB put **Josh Allen (45), Christian Watson (44), Ashton Jeanty (41), and Zack Baun (35)** on the same card and printed a **315** kitty that made 250 look quaint. That’s not a hot streak — that’s four players who would’ve been a respectable team by themselves wearing one jersey. Ryan Towner’s Slumlords climbed from the early wreckage to **176.5** after Monday and still finished dead last: Gibbs’ **42** was a lighthouse in a fog of **Drake London 4, George Pickens 5, and Harold Fannin 5**. Survivor doesn’t care that you “fought back.” Off the bus. Juice: the nuclear four and a league-high water mark. Junk: a Gibbs 42 in a funeral; London/Pickens/Fannin quiet hours.

Bill brought **241** to a gunfight and still left with an L — and the TE board was a personal foul. Luke’s Saltese closed it **255–241**, fourteen points that will live rent-free next to the “all-time wins, zero rings” plaque. The humiliation wasn’t even the margin; it was the position battle. Luke started **Mike Gesicki for 23**. Bill started his high-draft-capital room and got **Tyler Warren 12** plus **Kyle Pitts 0** in the flex, with Brock Bowers riding pine for another zero. Gesicki alone outscored Warren and smoked the combined Warren+Pitts stack **23–12** — a no-name TE winning the week against a “premium” room. That’s how you go 0-1 with a roster that was supposed to bully people at the position. Juice: Saltese finishing the job; Gesicki’s 23. Junk: Bill’s TE tax, Pitts’ zero, 241 as a losing score.

Tim’s Divers dropped a clean **258.5** and reminded the dual-era champ that Week 1 doesn’t care about your résumé. The engine was the **Swift / Lamar / JJ** stack doing adult work while the rest of the board finished the job Monday made honest. Kyle’s Doubtpfizer landed at **237** — not a collapse into oblivion, just ugly-adjacent for a franchise that usually loses cute. And then there’s the chip you don’t cash: **Brian Burns started for 4**, which is not how “safe” DL is supposed to look on a losing card. Divers win, doubt deferred. Juice: Divers’ skill stack closing the week. Junk: Burns’ four-point apology.

matchups.scoreline: Valley Old Goats 254, Newman Lake Sleep Paralysis Demons 221
matchups.blurb: Heff’s Goats turned an early knife fight into a **254–221** statement after Monday, and the engine was borderline unfair. **T.J. Watt dropped 52** — a half-century on IDP — while **Derrick Henry stamped 43** like the ground still owed him money. Rymo’s Newman answered with real juice from Flowers and Hurts, then watched the alphas ghost the assignment: **A.J. Brown 5** and **Davante Adams 5** as starters. That’s ten combined from two WR1s while Watt alone outscored both of them by a career. 221 is a fine score in most leagues. Here it’s a handshake and a ‘tough one.’ Juice: Watt’s 52 and Henry’s 43. Junk: Brown + Adams totaling a single good TE game.

Jesse’s LAB posted **246** and made it look like a plan. Kellen “the Host” Olson’s Pocket finished **216.5** after selling Bo Nix for $10 FAAB and handing Goff the keys — a transaction that already had the group chat warming up. Then Monday delivered the roast that writes itself: **Jaylen Waddle started in the flex for 1 point.** One. The Host’s featured WR put up a single on fantasy TV and the board still had the nerve to look surprised at 216.5. Hosting duties that didn’t include actual receiving yards. Juice: LAB’s 246. Junk: Waddle’s 1; the Nix-for-FAAB hangover.

THE flip — and **Jacob Crisp’s first Wheels Up victory**. Rookie season, Week 1, Monday night heist: Hyper went from a **202.5** loss to a **259.5** win and stole Gavin’s board while the league was already writing Dongers’ win tweet. **Kenneth Walker III dropped 48** as the lead actor while the rest of the Hyper lineup finally showed up for the new franchise’s first column in the W. Dongers still hit **246.5** with Bijan and Olave at **34** each — a perfectly respectable losing score in this format’s cruel new math — and somehow lost a game they thought they’d already won. First wins don’t come prettier than a Monday erasure. Juice: Jacob’s first W; Walker’s 48; the 57-point Monday swing. Junk: 246.5 tasting like a losing score.

Nate’s Substation closed **193–180** after buying Bo Nix for $10 FAAB (still shopping Purdy, McLaurin, and Tuten on the block) — and **Nix started for 5** in his new colors, which is comedy enough before you even open Ultron’s card. Aga’s Ultron is the garage-sale roast Bill ordered: top-shelf draft capital, empty shelves, lonely QB heroics. **Ja’Marr Chase 3, James Cook 10, and Colston Loveland 0** hit the field as starters, then **Myles Garrett added a 0** on DL for the encore. That’s Aga’s top-3 totaling **13** while Caleb Williams’ **41** tried to drag a brick wall across the finish line. Sub gets over the hump; Ultron gets the tape. Juice: Substation getting the W. Junk: Chase/Cook/Loveland totaling 13; Garrett’s zero.

recaps.closer: Kitty to TTAB. Bus seat vacated by Slumlords. Jacob Crisp cashed his first WU win on Monday’s Hyper heist. Bill’s 0-1 with a 241 and a TE room that lost to Gesicki. Aga’s top-3 totaled 13. The Host started Waddle for a single. WWJDD: start your studs, ignore Fantrax IDP math, and don’t celebrate until the Monday board is empty.
